# OAuth clients for AI services

<EnterpriseAlert>

This feature requires Consul Enterprise.
Refer to the [enterprise feature matrix](/consul/docs/enterprise#consul-enterprise-feature-availability) for additional information.

</EnterpriseAlert>

Consul registers an OAuth client for a service whose `ai.role` is `ai-agent` or `mcp-server`, and uses that client when a mesh proxy exchanges a caller token for a token bound to the next service. A service whose role is `inference-model` does not get an OAuth client. Its fields are on the [`ai` service definition](/consul/docs/reference/service#ai). This page describes the cluster and service configuration that starts dynamic client registration (DCR) and on-behalf-of (OBO) token exchange.

Consul registers clients with IBM Security Verify. Each client authenticates with `private_key_jwt` and an inline JSON Web Key Set (JWKS).

## Requirements

Complete the following steps before you register an `ai-agent` or `mcp-server`:

1. Enable the `consul-ai` feature gate. Consul rejects a service registration that contains an `ai` block while the gate is off.

   ```shell-session
   $ consul operator feature set consul-ai true
   ```

1. Create exactly one ACL auth method with `Type` set to `oidc` and `EnableServiceDCR` set to `true`. Consul waits to register clients when the cluster has no flagged method or more than one flagged method. Refer to [`EnableServiceDCR`](/consul/docs/secure/acl/auth-method/oidc#enableservicedcr).

   The flagged method is the cluster identity provider. Set `OIDCDiscoveryURL`, `OIDCClientID`, and `OIDCClientSecret` on that method. Set `JWTSupportedAlgs` to `["ES256"]`. IBM Security Verify signs tokens with ES256, and this field defaults to RS256. Consul uses `OIDCClientID` and `OIDCClientSecret` as the bootstrap client that registers service clients. You can omit `AllowedRedirectURIs` when the method is used for service registration. Set a nonzero `MaxTokenTTL` on the auth method. That field is not part of `Config`, and Consul rejects an `oidc` method when it is unset. The [service registration example](/consul/docs/secure/acl/auth-method/oidc#example-configuration-for-service-client-registration) uses `1h`.

   Consul rejects an agent configuration block named `oauth.iam`. Configure the identity provider with the auth method.

1. Register the service with an [`ai`](/consul/docs/reference/service#ai) block whose `role` is `ai-agent` or `mcp-server`. You can set the block in a service definition file, the [catalog register API](/consul/api-docs/catalog#register-entity), or the [agent service register API](/consul/api-docs/agent/service#register-service).

   Consul registers clients for services in the `default` namespace and `default` partition. The KV record uses the service name, not the service ID. Consul does not register a second client for the connect-proxy sidecar. An `inference-model` registration uses the same feature gate and does not create a client or a KV record.

## Roles

The `ai.role` value selects which services receive a client.

| `role` | Sub-block | On-behalf-of credential |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ai-agent` | `agent` | Yes. The agent exchanges tokens for outbound calls. |
| `mcp-server` | `mcp_server` | No. The server is an audience for callers. |

Set the one sub-block that matches `role`. `inference-model` is not a client role. Configure it on the [service definition](/consul/docs/reference/service#inference_model).

## Audiences

An on-behalf-of audience is the identity of the next service in the call. Consul builds that map from explicit proxy upstreams in the `default` namespace, `default` partition, and local datacenter. For each of those upstreams, Consul uses the destination service's registered client ID. You do not set an audience list on the service definition.

Consul does not add an audience for a wildcard upstream, a centrally configured upstream, a prepared query, a peered service, a service in another datacenter, or a service outside the `default` namespace and partition.

## MCP calls from an AI agent

Set `agent.mcp` and register a connect sidecar for the agent. The local agent copies the `ai-agent` block onto that sidecar. Consul then opens a loopback listener at `http://127.0.0.1:<mcp.port>/mcp`. The port is `15101` when unset. A catalog registration of the application service creates the OAuth client and does not open this listener. Consul does not copy an `inference-model` or `mcp-server` block onto a sidecar.

The listener allows a tool call when a [service intention](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/service-intentions) names the MCP server as the destination and the agent as the source. The allow permission must set the HTTP path to exactly `/mcp` and match the `x-mcp-tool` header with `Exact` or `Regex`. The header value is the tool name. A `<server>__<tool>` prefix names the MCP server. Without that prefix, the intention destination is the server. Consul ignores permissions that use a different path or that omit an `x-mcp-tool` exact or regex match.

Set the connect proxy `mode` to `transparent` when `agent.mcp` is set. An intention that allows a tool does not add that MCP server as an on-behalf-of audience. Add an explicit upstream for each server whose client ID must be an audience.

Human-in-the-loop approval runs when the request includes the `x-mcp-hitl` header. Consul applies `mcp.hitl.approval_timeout` to those requests. The default is `60s`. Requests without the header skip approval.

The following configuration allows `billing-agent` to call the `billing.lookup` tool on `billing-tools`. Set the destination protocol to `http` first. The default protocol is `tcp`, and Consul rejects this L7 permission for a TCP destination. Refer to [service defaults](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/service-defaults).

```hcl
Kind = "service-defaults"
Name = "billing-tools"
Protocol = "http"
```

```hcl
Kind = "service-intentions"
Name = "billing-tools"
Sources = [
  {
    Name = "billing-agent"
    Permissions = [
      {
        Action = "allow"
        HTTP = {
          PathExact = "/mcp"
          Header = [
            {
              Name  = "x-mcp-tool"
              Exact = "billing.lookup"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## Registration state

Consul stores the registration record in the KV store at `oauth/<service>/state`. `<service>` is the service name. The `state` field is one of the following:

| `state` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PENDING` | Registration has started and is not finished. If the identity provider rejects the client, Consul retries and does not write a separate failure state. |
| `ACTIVE` | The identity provider accepted the client. Delivery of the on-behalf-of credential to an `ai-agent` can still be in progress. |
| `ROTATING` | Consul is rotating the client key. |
| `REVOKING` | The service was deregistered and Consul is removing the client. |

The record contains the OAuth client credential, including the private key. Deny `key:read` on the `oauth/` prefix to every token except the Consul server. Consul does not return this record from the HTTP API.
